title: How Much Does DocuSign Pricing 2026 Cost?
summary: DocuSign pricing structures vary significantly based on your monthly envelope volume and integration needs. Compare these tiers to select the right plan.
body_markdown:
## DocuSign pricing plans and feature limits


### Personal plan for solo users


At the Personal plan level, you are capped at 5 envelopes per month. If you're a freelance consultant signing more than one contract per week, you'll hit a hard wall before the month ends.


At $11 per month, this tier lacks basic custom branding, which means businesses must compromise on professional presentation to save on subscription costs. Your clients see DocuSign’s logo rather than your own, which potentially undermines the professional appearance of a high-value agreement.


### Standard plan for small teams


The IAM Starter plan operates on an annual fee of $480 per user (billed at $40 per month), which grants each user access to a fixed capacity of 100 envelope sends per year,


This upfront payment covers the entire year of service regardless of whether you send one document or ninety-nine.


By introducing a tiered efficiency model, the Standard plan ensures the cost per document drops as you approach the 100-envelope cap, rewarding consistent but strictly limited usage.


According to data from[esign.ai](https://www.esign.ai/blog/reason-for-docusign-price) , sending 25 envelopes results in an effective cost of $12 each, so users pay a significant premium for low-volume usage. This is a significant premium for your low-activity usage.

The figures in the table represent the amortized cost of your $300 investment based on actual consumption, so your per-unit expense fluctuates depending on how frequently you utilize the service.


If you only use a fraction of your 100-envelope allotment, your realized price per signature skyrockets.


The most efficient point occurs just before the "fair use" policy begins to apply surcharges for additional sends. This allows you to maximize your budget without triggering unexpected fees.


### DocuSign envelope limits for multiple user accounts


The 100-envelope cap applies per user rather than as a fixed ceiling shared across the entire account. If you add a second or third user to the IAM Starter plan, each user retains their own 100-envelope allowance per year.


This creates a diminishing return for every new team member invited to the platform.


A team of five users on the IAM Starter plan each retain their own 100-envelope allowance per year rather than sharing a single pool, so heavy individual users can still trigger overage fees independently.

### DocuSign Business Pro plan pricing and limits


Business Pro targets teams that require complex document logic, but it holds the same 100-envelope baseline as the Standard plan.


You pay $45 per user per month for Business Pro, billed annually, primarily for features like signer attachments and drawing fields rather than increased volume, meaning the plan is poorly suited for high-frequency workflows.


Activepieces uses a credit-based billing system that meters AI usage while offering unlimited flows on every plan. This ensures that builders aren't taxed for breaking work into smaller, more resilient modules, as a ten-step process costs the same to run as a two-step workaround.


This model allows teams to orchestrate DocuSign triggers without the meter running on every internal logic gate, as shown on the published pricing page where every plan includes unlimited flows.


$540 is the total cost, yet it strictly limits your account to 100 envelopes. This limit forces you to audit your automated triggers monthly to avoid unexpected billing spikes.


### Enterprise Pro for high-volume scaling


Enterprise Pro is the only tier that has negotiable envelope pools, which you'll need if you're processing more than 1,000 documents annually.


Because it removes the rigid 100-envelope ceiling found in lower tiers, it prevents the workflow stoppages that occur when a standard account reaches its limit mid-quarter. However, this flexibility comes with a requirement for direct sales intervention, removing the transparency of the self-service pricing model.
